clue.text: Crowd comes back having swallowed defeat — that's mature

indicators.note: whatever swallows something holds it inside, so one piece goes into the middle of another
coming back means returning the way you came, so the word is read right to left

parts.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
a defeat is a loss

explanation.surface: A football crowd heads home after a defeat, and the commentator praises their grown-up attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed crowd, BOM, wraps around the defeat to give B-LOSS-OM. 'Mature' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to develop and come into full flower, the same sense of growing up as the verb mature.

clue.text: Lie about soldier being promoted for a major job

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed around another

parts.note: to bask is to lie in the sun

indicators.note: in a down clue promotion moves something upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Someone tells a lie about a soldier's promotion to land an important posting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' is a verb meaning to lounge in the sun, not a falsehood, and GI is the standard shorthand for an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A big ask is an informal phrase for a demanding request or a hard task, something requiring a great deal of effort.

clue.text: Working class in good heart

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A cheerful portrait of the working class in good spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working class' looks like one social phrase but splits in two. In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on form means performing well and feeling confident, close to being in good heart or good spirits.

clue.text: Celebrities go after county that's abandoning young artist

indicators.note: going after means following, so this piece is placed second
to abandon is to leave behind, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: Surrey is an English county south of London
Y is an abbreviation for young
the A-list is the set of top celebrities

explanation.surface: Famous people trail a county that is losing its young artistic talent.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county just south of London. 'Young artist' looks like one phrase, but 'young' only supplies the letter that goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrealist is a painter of the Surrealism movement, such as Dalí or Magritte, so a specific kind of artist.

clue.text: Report back over small man's chest

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting over another comes first
going back means travelling the other way, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a boom is a loud report, like a gunshot
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A medical report describes a small man's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' means a bang, not a document. Moobs is jokey British slang, short for 'man boobs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Moobs is a slang blend of man and boobs, describing fleshy breasts on a male body, hence the chest.

clue.text: What a nepotist might do for poet

definitions.note: a verb phrase read as two words, push kin
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a nepotist would push (promote) kin (relatives)
second meaning: the great Russian writer of verse

explanation.surface: A question about what someone who favours relatives might get up to.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as two words, PUSH KIN, to see the nepotist at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pushkin was the great Russian poet who wrote Eugene Onegin, often called the founder of modern Russian literature.

clue.text: Poet penniless on drug reportedly; this might mask the smell

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so it comes first
something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by sound rather than spelling

parts.note: an example: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer of The Raven
having no pennies means being poor
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
said together the three pieces match the French-derived word for scented petals

explanation.surface: A broke poet on drugs needs something to cover up the smell.
explanation.walkthrough: POTPOURRI is said 'poh-poo-ree', so POE, POOR and E run together give the sound. The silent T and doubled R are the spelling trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri is a bowl of dried petals and spices placed in rooms to give off a pleasant scent that hides bad odours.

clue.text: Wise man cut the middle out

indicators.note: taking the middle out removes the central letter of the word

parts.note: to sever is to cut

explanation.surface: A wise man advises cutting out the middle man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' is a verb to be replaced by a synonym, not an instruction. SEVER has five letters, so its middle V goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A seer is a prophet or sage who sees the future, a person of wisdom and insight.

clue.text: Persevere to maintain a bird as pet

parts.note: to keep something is to maintain it
taken as written
a tit is a small songbird, here kept as a pet

explanation.surface: Advice to stick with the effort of keeping a bird at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads naturally as 'keep a tit', with the same letters regrouped into the phrase. Tits are common small birds in Britain, like the blue tit.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep at it is an idiom meaning to continue working steadily despite difficulty, which is what persevering means.

clue.text: One can feel pain in guts before death

indicators.note: coming before something means being placed ahead of it

parts.note: guts means courage or nerve
death is the end of life

explanation.surface: A grim picture of someone suffering stomach pain before dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' means courage, not intestines, and 'pain in guts' is a false phrase across the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve endings are the receptors in body tissue that detect stimuli, so each one is a thing able to sense hurt.

clue.text: Assistant rejects official scoring error

indicators.note: to reject is to send back, so the letters are turned around

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a match official
OG is an own goal, scoring into your own net

explanation.surface: A match assistant refuses to accept that the referee got a goal wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: OG, an own goal, is the scoring error. Both pieces are joined and then the whole lot is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A gofer is a junior helper who runs errands, so called because they 'go for' things, a lowly kind of assistant.

clue.text: Showing great energy, take sides in another upheaval

indicators.note: an upheaval throws everything into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
the sides of a word are its edges, its opening and closing letters

parts.note: the outside letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: Political activists, full of energy, pick sides in yet another revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take sides' looks like a single idiom, but it means the outer letters of 'take', which join 'another' before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the tear is an informal phrase for rushing about wildly or going on a spree, full of frantic activity.

clue.text: Funny short scene can be downloaded from computer

definitions.note: a description of the thing rather than a noun synonym

indicators.note: something funny is odd or peculiar, so the letters come out in a strange order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A comic sketch clip is available to download online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny short scene' reads as a comedy clip, but 'Funny' only tells you to rearrange the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenshot is an image file capturing what is displayed on a monitor, something saved and taken off a device.

clue.text: Affected when chip lacks length

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a flake is a small chip of something
L is the abbreviation for length

explanation.surface: A computer chip short of length is somehow affected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chip' suggests a computer part, but here it is a flake, a small broken piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected means put on or pretended, as in affected manners, so it is a synonym for false or sham.

clue.text: Delighted with news for coinage

parts.note: made up is British slang for very pleased
word means news, as in 'any word from them?'

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled at the news about new money being minted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coinage' suggests money but means inventing a word. 'Made up' as 'thrilled' is British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A coinage is a newly invented term or expression, which is exactly a word someone has invented.

clue.text: African haven for sailor — one rejecting all limits

indicators.note: a haven shelters whoever is in it, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a Liberian comes from Liberia in West Africa
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: An African country offers a safe harbour to a seafarer who rejects every restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haven' suggests a port, but it only tells you the sailor goes inside the African.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertarian believes in maximum personal freedom and minimal state control, so opposes restrictions placed on individuals.

clue.text: Doctor gave boy no parting words when travelling

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A doctor refuses to give a boy a farewell before his journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the subject of the sentence; it is a verb telling you to rework the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Bon voyage is the French farewell wishing someone a good journey, said to a person setting off on a trip.

clue.text: Change location — increases clicks

parts.note: to up something is to increase it
a clock's ticks are small clicks

explanation.surface: Moving a website to a new address boosts its visitor clicks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clicks' suggests web traffic, but it means the ticking of a clock. To up sticks is British informal for moving home.
explanation.definitionFit: To up sticks is a British idiom for leaving where you live and moving somewhere else, often suddenly.

clue.text: Break extraordinarily fine case for jewellery

indicators.note: a case surrounds what it holds, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece
something done extraordinarily departs from the usual, so the letters take an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging
a ring is an item of jewellery

explanation.surface: A burglar breaks an exceptionally fine jewellery case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jewellery case' reads as a box, but 'case for' is the container instruction and the jewellery is a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a rule or law is to breach or violate it, the same as breaking it.

clue.text: Fluid in fat person due to too much lying?

definitions.note: a cryptic description of a state rather than a synonym

indicators.note: something fluid flows and changes shape, so the letters are free to move

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A medical query: is fluid retention in an overweight person caused by lying around too much?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' reads as lying down, which fits the fat person, but it means telling lies. The question mark flags the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The playground chant 'liar, liar, pants on fire' taunts someone caught telling untruths, so burning trousers are the punishment for fibbing.

clue.text: Arrange list of performers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put things in order or in a row
second meaning: the bill of acts at a concert or festival

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the noun are written the same, so one phrase covers both a festival organiser's task and the poster.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to organise or set in a row; as a noun a festival line-up is the roster of acts appearing.

clue.text: Quiet safety instruction in car

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for 'be quiet!'

explanation.surface: A quiet word about safety while driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt up!' is a rude British way of telling someone to shut up, and also a road-safety slogan for wearing a seatbelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Belt up is both a blunt command to stop talking and the order to buckle a seatbelt before a journey.

clue.text: Old city moving right right right

indicators.note: moving a letter rightward shifts its place, so the order changes

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: An ancient city drifts ever further to the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: The triple 'right' reads as emphasis. The first is part of the instruction 'move right', the second is the letter R to be moved, and the last is the definition. Shift R one place right in TROY.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party, which sits on the political right wing.

clue.text: Big shot the Spanish value gets award from Sweden

parts.note: a nob is a toff or important person, British slang
el is Spanish for the
to prize something is to value it

explanation.surface: A Spanish VIP is honoured with a Swedish award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Value' is a verb here, not a noun. A nob is British slang for someone of high social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel Prizes are presented in Stockholm, funded by the Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel's will, honouring science, literature and peace.

clue.text: Relaxes as toff takes the mickey

indicators.note: read as T off, it tells you to remove that letter from the word

parts.note: taking the mickey is British slang for teasing

explanation.surface: An upper-class man relaxes by making fun of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toff' looks like a posh person but splits as T off. A toff is British slang for an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to loosen or lessen tension, so eases is the third-person form matching relaxes.

clue.text: Wife abandons quick examination

indicators.note: whatever abandons a place leaves it, so a letter departs from the word

parts.note: swift means quick
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A wife walks out after a hurried medical check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick examination' reads as one phrase, but 'quick' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sift through papers is a careful search or inspection, a noun use of the verb meaning to sort through.

clue.text: You are what you eat? They would certainly agree

parts.note: surface reading: the health slogan that diet shapes who you are
setter's reading: people who literally eat people are made of what they eat

explanation.walkthrough: The saying is meant as diet advice; taken literally, only people who eat other humans would find it exactly true.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who devour human flesh are made of human flesh, so for them the healthy-eating proverb is literally correct.

clue.text: Frank makes some spare time

indicators.note: some means only part, so the tail of the word is dropped

parts.note: overtime is extra time worked beyond normal hours

explanation.surface: A man named Frank carves out some free time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning open. Overtime is extra or spare time on top of normal hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly and without concealment, much as frank describes someone honest and direct.

clue.text: Singular small accessory for one's darling

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
wee is Scottish for small
a tie is a clothing accessory

explanation.surface: An unusual little gift chosen for a loved one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' reads as odd or remarkable, but it is the grammar abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetie is an affectionate term of endearment for a loved one, the same as calling them darling or sweetheart.

clue.text: A father goes on ground to find refreshment

indicators.note: going on means following after, so this piece is placed second

parts.note: sod is turf, the ground's surface
taken as written
pop is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A dad walks across the field looking for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue order is A, father, ground, but 'goes on' puts A and the father after the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda pop is a sweet fizzy soft drink, the sort of thing you buy as a refreshing beverage.
